text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

- A new opinion poll commissioned by the Conservative Party shows that 60 percent of those questioned want the state to take over the running of hospitals. Only 26 percent want county councils to remain in control of hospitals.

- Russia wants to develop huge oil and gas finds in the Barents and Kara Seas. The gas discovery lies in the Stokmanovskaja field in the Barents Sea near the border with Norway. Development of the prospects will require western technology and Russian authorities are willing to award concessions for the project.
- Norway's agreement with the European Union over salmon exports, cemented on July 1, has pushed up the price of the fish by two to three crowns per kilogramme.

- Finance companies are growing and are taking over new market shares. In the first half of the year loans for leasing increased by 20 percent. One reason for the strong growth is that companies are becoming more willing to take loans for leasing agreements than demanding ownership of capital goods such as machines and cars.

- Development of the Snoehvit gas field in the Barents Sea could become a reality in the next few years. Statoil evaluated possible development solutions in the summer and has decided to go further with the project, which could mean investment of around 20 billion crowns.

- MRT Micros, producer of technology products for the medical sector, has made a breakthrough in Asia. MRT has signed an agreement for a strategic partnership with the huge Japanese medical company Kameda Group.

- 1997 will be the best ever year for the hotel industry in the city of Trondheim in northern Norway. A new prognosis from the tourist board shows an equivalent of 700,000 overnight stays this year compared with 481,000 in 1996.
